src: Des Moines Register, 8 Jan 1922, p. 20, 'Children Uncover 2 Boxes; $1,024 in All' (Newspapers.com 131085664); wire copies Council Bluffs Nonpareil 9 Jan, Quad-City Times 12 Jan, Decorah 18 Jan 1922

set.tovw: Lead grade F: $1,024 recovered in 1922 (Register original and wire copies); ownership was uncertain
pinev: 1913 Winnebago atlas, Forest Twp T98N R24W: Andrew Branstad W part sec. 1 and M. E. Branstad 120 acres NE sec. 1 (SE of Leland), another M. E. tract S sec. 4. No E. F. Branstad on the 1913 plate, so the 'old homestead a mile east' is taken as the family's sec. 1 land.
The Register original confirms 'about a mile east of Leland' and that ownership of the $1,024 was uncertain; the 1913 plat's sec 1 Branstad land remains the placement.

set.tovw: Lead grade F: $580 recovered in 1916 (three papers, one Muscatine dispatch); nothing reported left
set.st: In May 1916 Mrs. Ruth Stevens of Grandview, cleaning her cellar, moved a barrel and found $580 in gold ($5 piece first, then the rest). An eccentric recluse who had lived on the place years before, not named, was believed to have hidden his savings there. Found 1916; the house is not identified. Pin is the village, not the house.
set.t: Recovered 1916; village house not identified (1915 Iowa census could name the Stevens lot). Urban/village: look only.
pinev: Placed from the source text: GNIS Grandview (house in or near the village, not named)
Three papers carry the same Muscatine dispatch; no house named.
